call_points.text: Export volumes expected to recover progressively from Q2FY27, with meaningful export growth for the full year.
Branded business realisations rose about 9% over Q4FY26, matching the price hike taken in Q1.
No further price hikes planned in Q2FY27; pricing to be reviewed as the paddy season unfolds in Q3.
Cash plus investments rose to ₹1,841 Cr from ₹1,281 Cr on lower working capital and higher accruals.
Traditional trade market share declined about 2 percentage points over Q1 last year.
Saudi distributor search ongoing; direct entity deferred, with wholesaler arrangement continuing meanwhile.
Domestic branded volume growth in Q4 reached 16%, supported by strong retail demand and market share gains.
Exports to the Middle East faced severe shipping and logistic bottlenecks due to regional geopolitical tensions.

operating_notes.text: Q4FY26 domestic branded basmati realization was around ₹79,000 to ₹80,000 per MT, and export realization was about ₹1,38,500 to ₹1,39,000 per MT.
India's FY26 basmati exports were 6.52 million tonnes worth ₹50,138 Cr and non-basmati 15.01 million tonnes worth ₹51,892 Cr.
Container rates from India's west coast to the Middle East rose more than tenfold from about US$500 to as much as US$5,000 per container during the disruption.
India Gate held about 41% e-commerce market share at end-June, around 10 percentage points ahead of the next competitor.
